verdicts.reasoning: Every item requires the pupil to carry out the computation, including the verification items. The direct items likewise demand a computed result -- "Ate Gab puts 3 ribbons in each of 15 bags. How many ribbons are in all the bags?" (key 45). No item is answerable by recognition alone.

One-step items multiply a single pair: "Maico puts 2 costumes in each of 2 bags" (key 4). Two-step items chain a second multiplication: "Riza bought 2 packs with 7 pencils in each pack. Each pencil costs P4" (key 56 = 2 x 7 x 4). Both ends of the stated range appear.

All items are equal-groups multiplication in context: "puts 2 ribbons in each of 12 bags" (key 24), "3 ribbons in each of 15 bags" (key 45). The keys are products, not sums or quotients, and the "each" language cues repeated equal groups.

Five items are priced in pesos and ask for an amount to pay: "Arnel wants to buy 10 running shoes that cost P4 each. How much does Arnel need to pay in all?" (key 40). These require multiplying a unit price by a count, including the two-step price-per-item-within-packs case at seed 64.
